result.topic_en: An English excerpt copied from a biography of Newton (Brewster), quoting Laplace's praise of the Principia, Halley's Latin verse, and the opening facts of Newton's birth.
result.transcription:
pag. 1. ... The philosopher, indeed, (the Marquis La Place), to
whom posterity will probably assign the place next to
Newton, has characterized the Principia as pre-eminent
above all the productions of human intellect;
and has thus divested of extravagance the con-
temporary encomium upon its author,
Nec fas est propius mortali attingere Divos
Halley.
So near the gods - man cannot nearer go.
Sir Isaac Newton was born at Woolsthorpe, a hamlet in the
parish of Colsterworth in Lincolnshire, about six miles south
of Grantham, on the 25th December O. S. 1642, exactly one
year after Galileo died, and was baptized at Colsterworth
on the 1st January 1642-3. His father, Mr. Isaac Newton,
died at the early age of thirty-six, a little more than a year
